findings.finding: Read all 14 pages of Klaus Bundies 2018 complete score, IMSLP508463, headed D-DS Mus.ms.334a. Slow chromatic contrapuntal sections alternate with three Allegros. Allegro passagework passes between all three violins; pp. 9–10, especially bars 8–25, combine semiquaver runs, string crossings, accidentals and offbeat entries. No sustained extreme register or virtuoso double-stop writing.

grade.basis: Hardest individual violin line is level 3 (upper intermediate, about ABRSM 6): fluent semiquavers, upper-position access and chromatic fingering, balanced by much slow writing. Add one ensemble level for exposed three-way chromatic suspensions, independent imitative entries and passing running figures without a bass instrument. The judgment covers the complete five-number Bundies layout including its concluding Adagio sections; movement-number grouping differs from the page metadata.

findings.finding: Read the complete musical pages in all four Breitkopf & Härtel parts, IMSLP924821–924824. Serenade is Andantino in A major; Humoreske is Vivace in F major with a contrasting lyrical middle section. Cello 1 repeatedly changes between bass, tenor and treble clefs, with thumb-position fingerings, exposed upper-register melody, chromatic slurred figures, trills and double stops. Cello 2 has substantial tenor-register running work; the lower parts also share articulated figures and double stops. The fourth part includes a scordatura instruction near the Serenade ending.

grade.basis: Cello 1 is pre-diploma level 6 (about RCM 10/ARSM): recurrent thumb-position melody and register shifts, chromatic passagework at Vivace, varied articulation and upper-register double stops require a developed cellist across both pieces. This is sustained technical demand rather than a single isolated high note. Retain level 6 overall without an ensemble uplift: blend, close intonation, coordinated pizzicato/arco changes and shared timing matter, but the mostly regular, clear textures do not independently justify level 7. Both pieces are considered; the Serenade is more lyrical and the longer Humoreske supplies the predominant lively pace.
